requires no prior sibling negotiation or imported custody key, then positively
witnesses its real explicit negotiation and durable projection. It commits its
baseline without fanout and explicitly drives each real sync/Have exchange before
observing custody. A passive observer cannot advance pending work when the
fixture deliberately has no autonomous recovery owner.
Manual requesters must also retain the normal reception scope and drain every
accepted conversation before pooled reuse; a DM-only callback cannot project
channel controls. The [reference message-action fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/message_action_reference.rs)
retains authenticated public recall and reaction projection even when its
explicit pull receives the signed effect before competing peer fanout.
For a single-shot permission assertion, complete the real signed-discovery cache
before starting the listener. Adding a peer to the live roster alone does not
stabilize the persisted proof revision observed by finite sync views. The
`joined_group_protocol_snapshot_is_stable_before_single_shot_sync` control runs
the actual cache owner at view capture and requires an unchanged revision;
the original full-host scenario retains group access and DM/call rejection.
Keep genuine authority-change invalidation intact rather than retrying over it.

Keep fixture validation at the narrow boundary it owns. A full-host scenario
whose only assertion concerns another test helper adds unrelated synchronization
and scheduling prerequisites without a product oracle. Reuse the real protocol
and business scenarios instead: [Wake authentication and recovery controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
own linked identity, revision deduplication and notification-driven convergence;
[custody scenarios](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
own authenticated preparation, held-domain independence and durable custody.
Custody accounting preparation uses serial real channel-document requests on
inbound-only peers before autonomous workers start. A mutable whole-Optional or
Wake-settled snapshot is not a prerequisite for that accounting contract: it can
restart and create unrelated capacity contention while an observer waits. Remove
the global observer and its helper-only full-host tests; retain signed channel
floors, exact-peer capabilities and the real automatic custody/offline controls.
Qualify custody completion through the exact holder's durable reception witness. Durable ciphertext custody does not prove
that the independent plaintext projection is visible. Observe that projection
within the same existing functional deadline and retain unrelated protocol holds
through its business assertions. Preserve completed setup evidence for unchanged
peers and corpus; invalidate it before an actual topology withdrawal, rather than
discarding a completed comparison after reannouncing the same routes. The
held-directory custody and reference self-control fixtures own these boundaries.
A best-effort retry turn can return `None` after deferral or an exchange error;
keep the existing recovery owner and functional convergence budget while
preserving shared-negative, journal-migration and distinct-member count oracles.
Do not add a clock switch solely to rescue a helper's self-test. Keep a loopback
business scenario focused on its named behavior. The member-invitation proof
ends after epoch delivery, pre-join isolation and role rejection. Existing
focused transfer/authority controls own ownership changes; the small two-node
departure proof owns actual offline pause/relaunch and retry of the original
signed event and parent cut. Do not chain unrelated controls and reconnection
requirements onto an already complete invitation scenario.

Desktop archive fixtures must use the same account-owned channel genesis as the
desktop creation command and assert its owner before seeding content. Legacy
device-only genesis starts a separately consented background authority migration;
it cannot stand in for the desktop factory. The
[cloud archive command regression](../src-tauri/src/google_drive/command_tests.rs)
owns this production-path precondition and preserves real file/archive/restart
acceptance; core channel-maintenance tests own legacy migration.

A fixture with a live authoritative identity observer must not simulate account
replacement by changing only a derived UI store. A later valid backend observation
can restore that store. Keep the [startup browser proof](../frontend/e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts)
focused on startup and real logout/relogin; the [scoped pack](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts)
and [linked appearance](../frontend/src/lib/linkedAppearance.test.ts) controls own
replacement and stale callbacks. A browser test of an actual account transition
must change its authoritative identity boundary consistently.

Keep a scheduling control's corpus at the protocol boundary it needs. The
[queued-source controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/selected_queued_source_control_latency.rs)
use a normal short partial page and retain strict result/checkpoint ordering;
separate real-protocol tests own full-page durability and replay. Qualify request
liveness before its cancellation trigger and the actual resumed owner before
admission. A cancellation-triggering publication need not leave the old request
alive after the publisher returns.
The queued A-side paired hold must bind the scheduler's actual `paid_resume`
dispatch to its exact live child task. Same-source foreground replacements can also carry
the resumed/protected trace labels; those labels cannot certify a paid parked
turn or trigger its before-B ordering assertion. Retain the classifier's negative
foreground control and the real queued Noise scenarios under core-account-group
validation. A cross-peer interrupted unpaired continuation retains its distinct
live/resumed/protected admission proof; it does not spend paired resume credit.

Keep browser lifecycle fixtures at the smallest valid corpus that exercises their
contract, with separate inventory coverage for full archives. The
[sticker removal fixture](../frontend/e2e/stickers.spec.ts) imports one unchanged
animated asset through the real ZIP path, verifies its sent bytes before and
after removal, and checks persisted removal after one cold navigation. Its
installation and panel scenarios retain the complete pack. Avoid a redundant
reload immediately before a helper that already navigates; preserve the scenario
deadline and the persistence assertion.

Browser device options express intent; they do not observe native input state.
Establish the required device mode through the browser's supported emulation
owner, then verify actual media queries and touch capabilities before measuring
responsive hit areas. Do not replace `matchMedia` with a JavaScript mock. The
[touch fixture](../frontend/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts) exercises controlled native
state loss, actual CSS target sizes and a real tap through that same owner.
A negative control must observe the capability it removes; disabling touch does
not require every host to become hover-capable or shrink its CSS targets.

Before holding unrelated work in a full-host regression, observe the listener's
actual accept admission. Spawning a child is not proof it has been polled; work
in a scheduler-local slot may remain unavailable to other workers. Keep startup
readiness separate from the measured held-work progress condition.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.
For an ephemeral UDP endpoint, let the real socket owner bind port zero and
report the selected port. A released reservation is not ownership; reusable
discovery sockets can silently share the selected port with another runtime.
Participant preparation owns the actual IPv4/IPv6 port, and
`runtime_zero_discovery_port_owns_a_reachable_assigned_endpoint` in
[routed runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_routed_tests.rs)
requires distinct assigned endpoints and a real signed discovery response.

Intentional cancellation and output-limit controls need an independent process
owner. Inheriting the real runner's owner marker can terminate the enclosing
validation instead of only the synthetic command. The
[process-owner fixture](../scripts/diagnostics/windows-process-owner.test.mjs)
checks both the retained output-limit failure and successful enclosing supervisor
through an actual nested execution. When an assertion parses a child test report,
select its reporter explicitly; terminal detection must not change the machine
contract between TAP and human-readable output.

Executable process fixtures must copy their image and assert independent file
identity; a hard link aliases the live harness outside the child process owner.
The process-owner and release-reuse fixtures share bounded filesystem cleanup
after verified retirement, with a Windows held-image control that still rejects
a persistent lock and succeeds only after release.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Saved-login verification controls must select a complete credential policy, including
failed-login cleanup and migration compensation. A mock that skips biometric reads
does not prove the OS will not ask to authorize a changed application binary. The
[desktop credential owner](../src-tauri/src/session_store.rs) and
[startup policy](../src-tauri/src/settings/startup.rs) keep convenience recovery away
from Keychain on success and failure. Their controls cover stale local passwords,
retired writes and locking during provider replacement; native acceptance additionally
requires two packaged builds with different code identities. Verify actual prompts,
not merely the absence of an explicit authentication call.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or
the absence of every deadlock. Cancelled, interrupted, empty and unavailable runs
remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Verification collectors must release cancelled workflows while still rejecting
upstream failures. An unconditional collector can retain a cancelled candidate
and block its replacement in the concurrency group. The
[CI maintenance guide](ci-maintenance.md) owns this scheduling rule;
[merge-queue regressions](../scripts/diagnostics/merge-queue.test.mjs) exercise
eligibility after failure and ineligibility after cancellation. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.

Bounded subprocess output discovery must fail on truncation, not infer an empty
patch from a saturated buffer. Size Git diff transport for the supported source
boundary and exercise a real committed patch above the default buffer. Accepted
source promotion requires the existing exact main-push evidence owner plus live
source revalidation, not a local reference, PR-only green status or a coverage
threshold waiver. The [CI maintenance owner](ci-maintenance.md#synchronizing-an-accepted-main-source-into-dev),
`patch-coverage.test.mjs` and `pr-main-promotion.test.mjs` own these controls.

Dependency verification scope must bind identity to the actual tested merge and
consumer boundary, not only a bot author or version label. Independently revalidate
reduced profiles and require every selected producer's terminal success. External
coverage publication is a separate permission boundary from test execution; never
make missing bot credentials look like a product regression. The
[CI maintenance owner](ci-maintenance.md#dependabot-development-acceptance) and
`ci-docs-scope.test.mjs` / `ci-latency.test.mjs` own exact-source, mixed/native,
lockfile and failed/cancelled/missing-result controls.

Native failure evidence must include the actual release logger, not only captured
stdout. The [native capture owner](../scripts/diagnostics/native-capture.mjs) reads
bounded private file-log tails only after child retirement, preserves the original
failure when diagnostics are unavailable and rejects linked paths. Its filesystem
controls retain quotas, current-log priority and cutoff redaction. A responsive
failure screenshot or generic IPC timeout alone cannot identify a backend lock or
startup error; keep missing evidence distinct from a confirmed mechanism.

## Review record

For applicable risks, make these answers reviewable in the PR or task result:

- **Owner and invariant:** which implementation and authoritative rule apply?
- **Risks:** which rule IDs apply, and what reachable failure path was checked?
- **Progress and lifetime:** what can wait, what stays available, and who owns work
  after cancellation, retirement or retry?
- **Commit and authority:** what becomes durable, what invalidates permission,
  and how are stale or partially completed effects handled?
- **Evidence:** which regression/scenario exercised the boundary on which source,
  and what actually passed, failed or remained unverified?

Use concrete paths, operations and assertions. “Thread safe,” “handles errors,”
“tests pass” and checked boxes without evidence are not sufficient explanations.
For a nonapplicable risk, a short reason is enough; do not manufacture tests or
ceremonial reports for unrelated concerns.

## Keep the guide useful as defects are found

The author of a confirmed defect fix owns the corresponding guidance update;
the reviewer checks it alongside the regression and owning contract. Follow the
[requirement maintenance loop](testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

1. Identify the missing general decision, not just the incident's file or symptom.
   Strengthen an existing rule when it already covers the mechanism.
2. Add a new stable rule ID only for a distinct, reusable failure pattern. Include
   **trigger, failure mechanism, required approach, authoritative owner and
   observable regression evidence**. Add its route to the selection table.
3. Update the owning implementation/guide and affected `validation.json` selectors,
   consumers or scenarios when needed. A prose reminder cannot replace the test
   or make an unselected regression part of future checks.
4. Maintain example links when code moves; update rule references when rules merge
   or retire. Do not silently reuse an ID for a different meaning. Remove obsolete
   advice rather than appending conflicting exceptions or dated status updates.

Keep this a compact set of reusable decisions. Do not add test-count histories,
commit diaries, machine-specific commands or a parallel copy of feature contracts.
Unconfirmed suspicions belong in an issue or ignored investigation notes. This
guide supports engineering judgment and executable validation; it cannot make
unreviewed generated code reliable by itself.

# Dispatching Parallel Agents

## Overview

You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

When you have multiple unrelated failures (different test files, different subsystems, different bugs), investigating them sequentially wastes time. Each investigation is independent and can happen in parallel.

**Core principle:** Dispatch one agent per independent problem domain. Let them work concurrently.

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Multiple failures?" [shape=diamond];
    "Are they independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Single agent investigates all" [shape=box];
    "One agent per problem domain" [shape=box];
    "Can they work in parallel?" [shape=diamond];
    "Sequential agents" [shape=box];
    "Parallel dispatch" [shape=box];

    "Multiple failures?" -> "Are they independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Single agent investigates all" [label="no - related"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Can they work in parallel?" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Parallel dispatch" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Sequential agents" [label="no - shared state"];
}
```

**Use when:**
- 3+ test files failing with different root causes
- Multiple subsystems broken independently
- Each problem can be understood without context from others
- No shared state between investigations

**Don't use when:**
- Failures are related (fix one might fix others)
- Need to understand full system state
- Agents would interfere with each other

## The Pattern

### 1. Identify Independent Domains

Group failures by what's broken:
- File A tests: Tool approval flow
- File B tests: Batch completion behavior
- File C tests: Abort functionality

Each domain is independent - fixing tool approval doesn't affect abort tests.

### 2. Create Focused Agent Tasks

Each agent gets:
- **Specific scope:** One test file or subsystem
- **Clear goal:** Make these tests pass
- **Constraints:** Don't change other code
- **Expected output:** Summary of what you found and fixed

### 3. Dispatch in Parallel

```typescript
// In Claude Code / AI environment
Task("Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts failures")
Task("Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts failures")
Task("Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts failures")
// All three run concurrently
```

### 4. Review and Integrate

When agents return:
- Read each summary
- Verify fixes don't conflict
- Run full test suite
- Integrate all changes

## Agent Prompt Structure

Good agent prompts are:
1. **Focused** - One clear problem domain
2. **Self-contained** - All context needed to understand the problem
3. **Specific about output** - What should the agent return?

```markdown
Fix the 3 failing tests in src/agents/agent-tool-abort.test.ts:

1. "should abort tool with partial output capture" - expects 'interrupted at' in message
2. "should handle mixed completed and aborted tools" - fast tool aborted instead of completed
3. "should properly track pendingToolCount" - expects 3 results but gets 0

These are timing/race condition issues. Your task:

1. Read the test file and understand what each test verifies
2. Identify root cause - timing issues or actual bugs?
3. Fix by:
   - Replacing arbitrary timeouts with event-based waiting
   - Fixing bugs in abort implementation if found
   - Adjusting test expectations if testing changed behavior

Do NOT just increase timeouts - find the real issue.

Return: Summary of what you found and what you fixed.
```

## Common Mistakes

**❌ Too broad:** "Fix all the tests" - agent gets lost
**✅ Specific:** "Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts" - focused scope

**❌ No context:** "Fix the race condition" - agent doesn't know where
**✅ Context:** Paste the error messages and test names

**❌ No constraints:** Agent might refactor everything
**✅ Constraints:** "Do NOT change production code" or "Fix tests only"

**❌ Vague output:** "Fix it" - you don't know what changed
**✅ Specific:** "Return summary of root cause and changes"

## When NOT to Use

**Related failures:** Fixing one might fix others - investigate together first
**Need full context:** Understanding requires seeing entire system
**Exploratory debugging:** You don't know what's broken yet
**Shared state:** Agents would interfere (editing same files, using same resources)

## Real Example from Session

**Scenario:** 6 test failures across 3 files after major refactoring

**Failures:**
- agent-tool-abort.test.ts: 3 failures (timing issues)
- batch-completion-behavior.test.ts: 2 failures (tools not executing)
- tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts: 1 failure (execution count = 0)

**Decision:** Independent domains - abort logic separate from batch completion separate from race conditions

**Dispatch:**
```
Agent 1 → Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts
Agent 2 → Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts
Agent 3 → Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts
```

**Results:**
- Agent 1: Replaced timeouts with event-based waiting
- Agent 2: Fixed event structure bug (threadId in wrong place)
- Agent 3: Added wait for async tool execution to complete

**Integration:** All fixes independent, no conflicts, full suite green

**Time saved:** 3 problems solved in parallel vs sequentially

## Key Benefits

1. **Parallelization** - Multiple investigations happen simultaneously
2. **Focus** - Each agent has narrow scope, less context to track
3. **Independence** - Agents don't interfere with each other
4. **Speed** - 3 problems solved in time of 1

## Verification

After agents return:
1. **Review each summary** - Understand what changed
2. **Check for conflicts** - Did agents edit same code?
3. **Run full suite** - Verify all fixes work together
4. **Spot check** - Agents can make systematic errors

## Real-World Impact

From debugging session (2025-10-03):
- 6 failures across 3 files
- 3 agents dispatched in parallel
- All investigations completed concurrently
- All fixes integrated successfully
- Zero conflicts between agent changes
# Performance requirements

Read this before changing background work, synchronization, storage, caches or UI
state. Mesh Talk should cost little while waiting, load data when needed and stay
bounded as history grows. This guide owns cross-cutting performance requirements;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md), [network budgets](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and [reliability rules](ai-coding-reliability.md) own their implementation contracts.

## Budgets and measurement

These are initial project targets, **not industry standards or claims that the
current application meets them**. Establish a production-build baseline on each
supported platform. Reference fixture: 4 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, 100 contacts,
20 groups and 100,000 stored messages; no pending transfers, calls or animations.
Separate cold start, warm start, catch-up, visible idle and hidden idle. Measure a
quiet five-minute window after warmup; record build, runtime, profile and workload.
Warm startup restarts the process with OS caches retained; cold startup records
its uncached/first-launch conditions. Usable means an actionable list or
conversation, not a blank shell; report human authorization waits separately.
The empty-shell comparison keeps the same backend, runtime, process membership
and window settings, with user payloads absent.

| Resource                | Initial target for the reference fixture                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Idle CPU                | Visible desktop: ≤1% of one logical CPU; hidden desktop: ≤0.25%; headless node: ≤0.5%, averaged over the window.                                                                                    |
| Retained memory         | Headless node: ≤64 MiB private commit. Desktop: ≤64 MiB workload delta above the same-build empty shell; establish a reviewed whole-family ceiling from that baseline.                              |
| Memory growth           | Repeated navigation/media cycles reach a bounded plateau. Tenfold stored history must not require tenfold startup reads or retained UI payloads.                                                    |
| Idle writes             | Zero business-data commits for unchanged inputs. Target ≤5 MiB/hour OS-observed attributable storage writes per application family after warmup; measure the full hour before claiming this target. |
| Background wakeups      | No application maintenance timer without pending work, a real deadline or a documented recovery purpose. Noncritical recovery defaults to ≥5 minutes and coalesces activation.                      |
| Startup and interaction | First usable shell ≤1 s warm / ≤3 s cold; ordinary interaction must not run blocking I/O, crypto or an unbounded traversal on the UI thread. Report hydration/catch-up separately.                  |

CPU means `100 × process CPU seconds / wall seconds`, summed over the full app
family; divide by logical CPU count only when reporting whole-machine percent.
Report Rust host **and** renderer/GPU/helpers. Distinguish private commit, private
resident memory, shared pages and live JS heap; on Linux use PSS for shared-page
attribution. Logical I/O includes IPC/network activity and is not physical disk
I/O; OS disk events also do not measure physical NAND write amplification. CPU alone does not establish battery/power efficiency: inspect wakeups, GPU,
network and actual energy where supported. Keep metrics collected in different
windows separate. Store measurements in PR/CI artifacts, not this guide.

An existing target miss requires recorded baseline and an owned follow-up; it is
not permission to worsen the path or silently raise its budget. A target change
requires comparable evidence and review. Migrations, catch-up and active media have
separate bounded work budgets and progress evidence, not an unlimited exception.

## Apply to every feature

Before implementation, identify the owning producer, its meaningful trigger,
bounded work unit, retained resources and stop condition. Review all three phases,
including costs introduced in another process or on another device:

| Phase           | Required design and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Startup         | Load indexed summaries and the active conversation's bounded page first. Defer inactive history, attachment bytes and optional features until demanded. Avoid decrypting all history, rebuilding unchanged indexes or republishing unchanged state at each login. Measure time to usable UI, peak memory, bytes read and writes separately from catch-up; migrations need resumable bounded progress.                    |
| Idle            | With unchanged inputs, settle business producers and avoid business-data writes. Use scoped events and exact next deadlines; coalesce noncritical repair into the existing serial queue, normally at least five minutes apart. A heartbeat, read, empty reply or offline device must not restart historical work. Verify visible and hidden states, including renderer/helpers and remote work triggered by this client. |
| Active business | Bound each query, decrypt, decode, transfer and rendering turn by items and bytes. Drain real available work promptly with backpressure and cancellation; user interaction and reception must remain responsive. Measure latency, peak CPU/memory and I/O for send/receive, catch-up, search, media and navigation as applicable, then prove resources settle when work finishes.                                        |

Do not classify a permanently retrying historical queue as an unlimited active
workload. Distinguish actionable progress from blocked work, record its outcome
and retain a bounded retry deadline. Successful reads, metadata comparisons and
already-held custody are not new user data. Serializing unnecessary work or
lengthening a timer alone does not establish that its cost is justified.

For every affected phase, the PR must state the trigger and stop condition,
resource bound, selected regression and measured result or explicit evidence gap.
Exercise unchanged inputs, growing history, unavailable dependencies and owner
replacement where applicable. Compare the same workload before and after; verify
return to idle and memory reclamation after repeated use. Do not infer low power
from a quiet disk, fast startup from a blank window, or bounded memory from one
snapshot. Existing misses remain explicit follow-ups with an owning module and
reproduction; never describe a passing correctness test as performance acceptance.

## Design and review rules

1. **Trigger work from meaning.** Prefer committed changes, scoped invalidations,
   user navigation and foreground activation. Schedule the next actual expiry or
   retry deadline. Empty success is not progress and must not keep a fast retry
   hot. Coalesce duplicate wakes; retain bounded dirty work while a task is busy.
   Pending work still owns its retry deadline. Suppress unchanged ordinary wakes
   using scheduling evidence, independently of successful completion; preserve
   explicit drivers and event-only progress when no timer owns continuation.
   A retained blocked task is not evidence of progress: keep its recovery fact
   while backing off, and resume promptly on dependency changes. Local pagination
   and actual received bytes retain prompt continuation.
   Reconfirming an already-held relay copy is not new progress. Park unchanged
   successful reconciliation until sparse repair; keep authenticated recipient
   delivery and actual custody-loss recovery separate from that scheduling hint.
   A bounded historical scan must also become quiet after its complete sweep;
   preserve prompt unfinished pages and separate lightweight claim rechecks.
   Qualify scan completion against current source and semantic inputs, before
   and after work. Failed discovery keeps a separate bounded wait; it cannot
   acknowledge EOF or repeatedly hydrate the same blocked item on observer wakes.
   Preserve invalidation domains through batching and acknowledgement; a roster
   heartbeat must not reload unrelated settings or history. Empty pages do not
   imply a global change. Presentation metadata does not renew user activity.
   Keep semantic scope through auxiliary listeners too: document and sync-status
   changes must not query every group, and status-only changes must not reload
   document inventories. Mixed changes retain every affected domain; unknown
   inputs use conservative repair rather than silently dropping work.
   Retry fairness is scheduling state, not durable progress. Use a bounded
   runtime order where possible; retain durable pending/completion evidence and
   an explicit capacity fallback. Rechecking blocked work must not itself renew
   durable tickets indefinitely.
   Compare canonical endpoint sets rather than preferred-route order. Renewing
   an already-known route must not restart synchronization; actual topology,
   role, account and privacy changes retain their invalidations.
   Apply that projection consistently across retry, continuation and publication
   consumers; otherwise an unchanged observation can still reset another lane.
   Advance semantic revisions only when their authoritative value changes.
   Emit presentation invalidations only for changed facts; successful idempotent
   confirmation must not restart UI reads or persistence. Capture change evidence
   inside the committing owner and notify after releasing its guard.
   Subscribe to high-frequency observations in their small status surface rather
   than the message viewport's parent. A changed peer-check timestamp must update
   its own label without rebuilding unchanged virtualized rows; message, expiry
   and conversation/session changes retain their independent subscriptions.
   Notification context subscribes only to the active conversation and canonical
   matching device set. Peer freshness, names and unrelated roster changes must
   not clear and republish the same native context or rerender the chat shell.
   Replacing an identical binding map is not invalidation; actual removal and
   later restoration must each invalidate their preceding observation.
   Subscribe before the initial read, retain one follow-up for changes during
   work, and gate settled credential reconciliation before secret decoding and
   applied-marker I/O. Pending, locked and failed work retain recovery; event
   hints never replace fresh authorization at application and commit.
   Reuse identical intrinsic signature facts in a bounded metadata owner, keyed
   by every verification input and signature. Cache successful facts only; keep
   live identity, policy, revocation and freshness checks at their owning boundary.
   Contended or unavailable caches must not introduce a blocking dependency.

2. **Use recovery deliberately.** Ordinary fallback maintenance should drain a
   bounded, coalescing queue serially through its existing lifecycle owner.
   Prefer one admitted worker; justify additional parallelism with a concrete
   latency or progress requirement. Queue only relevant dirty work or due repair,
   deduplicate by scope and skip missed timer bursts. Bound each turn and rotate
   unfinished work fairly; an unavailable peer must not monopolize the queue.
   Keep synchronous I/O/crypto off the UI/async event thread, and retain capacity
   until the actual worker finishes even if its observer is cancelled. Preserve
   independent deadlines for transport leases, active delivery and real expiry;
   trace dependencies before sharing a worker to avoid cross-lane wait cycles.
   Serial execution bounds peaks; unchanged inputs must still avoid the work.
   Retire superseded producers when consolidating maintenance. Check the actual

progress budget, and that budget must still cancel actual owned work.

A storage fault fixture must fail the currently selected persistence owner and
observe that failure before asserting recovery. A hook on a neighboring journal
cannot certify the actual commit failed merely because both use the same logger.

A bounded positive observer may keep waiting on the owning API's explicit pending
state. Match only that state; storage, authorization and unexpected failures stay
fatal. Preserve the original deadline and exact outcome assertions. Prior readiness
is not a lease: live sibling attachment recovery can invalidate a canonical history
projection between polls. The existing `ready_history` owner in
[`node_tests.rs`](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/node_tests.rs) preserves
`StaleCursor` as pending and distinguishes a ready empty history; its storage and
authorization controls remain fatal. Indexed queries on an acquired projection
can themselves become stale after a concurrent append; propagate those results
through the same pending-state classifier instead of unwrapping inside a match
guard. Keep real checkpoint invalidation/reacquisition and automatic/manual
departure recovery controls alongside the linked-device reconnect and
classification tests.
The source's positive message observation uses the same pending-state owner;
source readiness and sibling delivery share the original delivery deadline.
Custody fixtures identify the exact outgoing body and sender through that owner:
source identification shares the existing holder-setup deadline or the already-offline
sibling-delivery deadline. A successful read while producers remain live is a
snapshot; retain its witnessed rows for the immediate assertion rather than
unwrapping a fresh read. Joined producer retirement is a different boundary.
Self-control Noise setup likewise waits for the source archive marker through
`StaleCursor` within its existing shared cold deadline, before measuring the action.
The [two-parent control fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/channels.rs)
also preserves the metadata publisher's precommit source guard: only its explicit `StaleCursor` can retry during the original setup
deadline. Keep revision conflicts, storage and authorization failures fatal, and
retain the later signed-value and unchanged-source/work assertions.
An authenticated completion describes its response epoch, not a permanently
frozen source. Exact metadata comparisons in the
[control-page fixtures](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/sync.rs)
own their controlled publication epochs under the
[protocol fixture contract](testing-feedback-loop.md#protocol-fixture-response-epochs);
retain separate live-provider mutation and re-comparison coverage.
Timeout diagnostics retain pending/error results instead of unwrapping another
history query and masking the primary failure.

An offline fixture that needs prompt connection failure must own and observe
actual transport closure; reserving a TCP port does not guarantee refusal or
retire a pending dial. The [own-copy fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime_tests.rs)
qualifies real accept-and-close behavior, joins its unavailable-endpoint owner,
then hands the same listener to the cold application without changing its
confirmation budget.

A direct protocol fixture must own its cold-start preconditions. Starting every
background repair loop can negotiate or import the claimed first request before
the explicit operation and consume its transport capacity. Reuse the bounded
[inbound connection owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/serving.rs) when the
scenario drives requests directly; keep full-host recovery tests separate. The
[certificate refresh fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
requires no prior sibling negotiation or imported custody key, then positively
witnesses its real explicit negotiation and durable projection. It commits its
baseline without fanout and explicitly drives each real sync/Have exchange before
observing custody. A passive observer cannot advance pending work when the
fixture deliberately has no autonomous recovery owner.
Manual requesters must also retain the normal reception scope and drain every
accepted conversation before pooled reuse; a DM-only callback cannot project
channel controls. The [reference message-action fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/message_action_reference.rs)
retains authenticated public recall and reaction projection even when its
explicit pull receives the signed effect before competing peer fanout.
For a single-shot permission assertion, complete the real signed-discovery cache
before starting the listener. Adding a peer to the live roster alone does not
stabilize the persisted proof revision observed by finite sync views. The
`joined_group_protocol_snapshot_is_stable_before_single_shot_sync` control runs
the actual cache owner at view capture and requires an unchanged revision;
the original full-host scenario retains group access and DM/call rejection.
Keep genuine authority-change invalidation intact rather than retrying over it.

Keep fixture validation at the narrow boundary it owns. A full-host scenario
whose only assertion concerns another test helper adds unrelated synchronization
and scheduling prerequisites without a product oracle. Reuse the real protocol
and business scenarios instead: [Wake authentication and recovery controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
own linked identity, revision deduplication and notification-driven convergence;
[custody scenarios](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
own authenticated preparation, held-domain independence and durable custody.
Custody accounting preparation uses serial real channel-document requests on
inbound-only peers before autonomous workers start. A mutable whole-Optional or
Wake-settled snapshot is not a prerequisite for that accounting contract: it can
restart and create unrelated capacity contention while an observer waits. Remove
the global observer and its helper-only full-host tests; retain signed channel
floors, exact-peer capabilities and the real automatic custody/offline controls.
Qualify custody completion through the exact holder's durable reception witness. Durable ciphertext custody does not prove
that the independent plaintext projection is visible. Observe that projection
within the same existing functional deadline and retain unrelated protocol holds
through its business assertions. Preserve completed setup evidence for unchanged
peers and corpus; invalidate it before an actual topology withdrawal, rather than
discarding a completed comparison after reannouncing the same routes. The
held-directory custody and reference self-control fixtures own these boundaries.
A best-effort retry turn can return `None` after deferral or an exchange error;
keep the existing recovery owner and functional convergence budget while
preserving shared-negative, journal-migration and distinct-member count oracles.
Do not add a clock switch solely to rescue a helper's self-test. Keep a loopback
business scenario focused on its named behavior. The member-invitation proof
ends after epoch delivery, pre-join isolation and role rejection. Existing
focused transfer/authority controls own ownership changes; the small two-node
departure proof owns actual offline pause/relaunch and retry of the original
signed event and parent cut. Do not chain unrelated controls and reconnection
requirements onto an already complete invitation scenario.

Desktop archive fixtures must use the same account-owned channel genesis as the
desktop creation command and assert its owner before seeding content. Legacy
device-only genesis starts a separately consented background authority migration;
it cannot stand in for the desktop factory. The
[cloud archive command regression](../src-tauri/src/google_drive/command_tests.rs)
owns this production-path precondition and preserves real file/archive/restart
acceptance; core channel-maintenance tests own legacy migration.

A fixture with a live authoritative identity observer must not simulate account
replacement by changing only a derived UI store. A later valid backend observation
can restore that store. Keep the [startup browser proof](../frontend/e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts)
focused on startup and real logout/relogin; the [scoped pack](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts)
and [linked appearance](../frontend/src/lib/linkedAppearance.test.ts) controls own
replacement and stale callbacks. A browser test of an actual account transition
must change its authoritative identity boundary consistently.

Keep a scheduling control's corpus at the protocol boundary it needs. The
[queued-source controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/selected_queued_source_control_latency.rs)
use a normal short partial page and retain strict result/checkpoint ordering;
separate real-protocol tests own full-page durability and replay. Qualify request
liveness before its cancellation trigger and the actual resumed owner before
admission. A cancellation-triggering publication need not leave the old request
alive after the publisher returns.
The queued A-side paired hold must bind the scheduler's actual `paid_resume`
dispatch to its exact live child task. Same-source foreground replacements can also carry
the resumed/protected trace labels; those labels cannot certify a paid parked
turn or trigger its before-B ordering assertion. Retain the classifier's negative
foreground control and the real queued Noise scenarios under core-account-group
validation. A cross-peer interrupted unpaired continuation retains its distinct
live/resumed/protected admission proof; it does not spend paired resume credit.

Keep browser lifecycle fixtures at the smallest valid corpus that exercises their
contract, with separate inventory coverage for full archives. The
[sticker removal fixture](../frontend/e2e/stickers.spec.ts) imports one unchanged
animated asset through the real ZIP path, verifies its sent bytes before and
after removal, and checks persisted removal after one cold navigation. Its
installation and panel scenarios retain the complete pack. Avoid a redundant
reload immediately before a helper that already navigates; preserve the scenario
deadline and the persistence assertion.

Browser device options express intent; they do not observe native input state.
Establish the required device mode through the browser's supported emulation
owner, then verify actual media queries and touch capabilities before measuring
responsive hit areas. Do not replace `matchMedia` with a JavaScript mock. The
[touch fixture](../frontend/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts) exercises controlled native
state loss, actual CSS target sizes and a real tap through that same owner.
A negative control must observe the capability it removes; disabling touch does
not require every host to become hover-capable or shrink its CSS targets.

Before holding unrelated work in a full-host regression, observe the listener's
actual accept admission. Spawning a child is not proof it has been polled; work
in a scheduler-local slot may remain unavailable to other workers. Keep startup
readiness separate from the measured held-work progress condition.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.
For an ephemeral UDP endpoint, let the real socket owner bind port zero and
report the selected port. A released reservation is not ownership; reusable
discovery sockets can silently share the selected port with another runtime.
Participant preparation owns the actual IPv4/IPv6 port, and
`runtime_zero_discovery_port_owns_a_reachable_assigned_endpoint` in
[routed runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_routed_tests.rs)
requires distinct assigned endpoints and a real signed discovery response.

Intentional cancellation and output-limit controls need an independent process
owner. Inheriting the real runner's owner marker can terminate the enclosing
validation instead of only the synthetic command. The
[process-owner fixture](../scripts/diagnostics/windows-process-owner.test.mjs)
checks both the retained output-limit failure and successful enclosing supervisor
through an actual nested execution. When an assertion parses a child test report,
select its reporter explicitly; terminal detection must not change the machine
contract between TAP and human-readable output.

Executable process fixtures must copy their image and assert independent file
identity; a hard link aliases the live harness outside the child process owner.
The process-owner and release-reuse fixtures share bounded filesystem cleanup
after verified retirement, with a Windows held-image control that still rejects
a persistent lock and succeeds only after release.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Saved-login verification controls must select a complete credential policy, including
failed-login cleanup and migration compensation. A mock that skips biometric reads
does not prove the OS will not ask to authorize a changed application binary. The
[desktop credential owner](../src-tauri/src/session_store.rs) and
[startup policy](../src-tauri/src/settings/startup.rs) keep convenience recovery away
from Keychain on success and failure. Their controls cover stale local passwords,
retired writes and locking during provider replacement; native acceptance additionally
requires two packaged builds with different code identities. Verify actual prompts,
not merely the absence of an explicit authentication call.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or
the absence of every deadlock. Cancelled, interrupted, empty and unavailable runs
remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Verification collectors must release cancelled workflows while still rejecting
upstream failures. An unconditional collector can retain a cancelled candidate
and block its replacement in the concurrency group. The
[CI maintenance guide](ci-maintenance.md) owns this scheduling rule;
[merge-queue regressions](../scripts/diagnostics/merge-queue.test.mjs) exercise
eligibility after failure and ineligibility after cancellation. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.

Bounded subprocess output discovery must fail on truncation, not infer an empty
patch from a saturated buffer. Size Git diff transport for the supported source
boundary and exercise a real committed patch above the default buffer. Accepted
source promotion requires the existing exact main-push evidence owner plus live
source revalidation, not a local reference, PR-only green status or a coverage
threshold waiver. The [CI maintenance owner](ci-maintenance.md#synchronizing-an-accepted-main-source-into-dev),
`patch-coverage.test.mjs` and `pr-main-promotion.test.mjs` own these controls.

Dependency verification scope must bind identity to the actual tested merge and
consumer boundary, not only a bot author or version label. Independently revalidate
reduced profiles and require every selected producer's terminal success. External
coverage publication is a separate permission boundary from test execution; never
make missing bot credentials look like a product regression. The
[CI maintenance owner](ci-maintenance.md#dependabot-development-acceptance) and
`ci-docs-scope.test.mjs` / `ci-latency.test.mjs` own exact-source, mixed/native,
lockfile and failed/cancelled/missing-result controls.

Native failure evidence must include the actual release logger, not only captured
stdout. The [native capture owner](../scripts/diagnostics/native-capture.mjs) reads
bounded private file-log tails only after child retirement, preserves the original
failure when diagnostics are unavailable and rejects linked paths. Its filesystem
controls retain quotas, current-log priority and cutoff redaction. A responsive
failure screenshot or generic IPC timeout alone cannot identify a backend lock or
startup error; keep missing evidence distinct from a confirmed mechanism.

## Review record

For applicable risks, make these answers reviewable in the PR or task result:

- **Owner and invariant:** which implementation and authoritative rule apply?
- **Risks:** which rule IDs apply, and what reachable failure path was checked?
- **Progress and lifetime:** what can wait, what stays available, and who owns work
  after cancellation, retirement or retry?
- **Commit and authority:** what becomes durable, what invalidates permission,
  and how are stale or partially completed effects handled?
- **Evidence:** which regression/scenario exercised the boundary on which source,
  and what actually passed, failed or remained unverified?

Use concrete paths, operations and assertions. “Thread safe,” “handles errors,”
“tests pass” and checked boxes without evidence are not sufficient explanations.
For a nonapplicable risk, a short reason is enough; do not manufacture tests or
ceremonial reports for unrelated concerns.

## Keep the guide useful as defects are found

The author of a confirmed defect fix owns the corresponding guidance update;
the reviewer checks it alongside the regression and owning contract. Follow the
[requirement maintenance loop](testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

1. Identify the missing general decision, not just the incident's file or symptom.
   Strengthen an existing rule when it already covers the mechanism.
2. Add a new stable rule ID only for a distinct, reusable failure pattern. Include
   **trigger, failure mechanism, required approach, authoritative owner and
   observable regression evidence**. Add its route to the selection table.
3. Update the owning implementation/guide and affected `validation.json` selectors,
   consumers or scenarios when needed. A prose reminder cannot replace the test
   or make an unselected regression part of future checks.
4. Maintain example links when code moves; update rule references when rules merge
   or retire. Do not silently reuse an ID for a different meaning. Remove obsolete
   advice rather than appending conflicting exceptions or dated status updates.

Keep this a compact set of reusable decisions. Do not add test-count histories,
commit diaries, machine-specific commands or a parallel copy of feature contracts.
Unconfirmed suspicions belong in an issue or ignored investigation notes. This
guide supports engineering judgment and executable validation; it cannot make
unreviewed generated code reliable by itself.
"}

# Media send transitions implementation plan

Goal: Replace the recorded fallback-emoji/loading/waiting jumps with stable artwork, a single quiet transfer state and short truthful transitions.

Architecture: Keep protocol and receipt authorities unchanged. An owner-scoped bounded outgoing-preview store supplies only locally captured ordinary image/sticker bytes to visible outgoing rows by their existing clientId. Media components retain their geometry and fade from that temporary preview to the durable decoded source; generic attachments use their existing secondary line for status. Existing transfer observations drive percentages.

Stack: React, Zustand, the current media cache/hooks, CSS opacity/transform transitions and existing Framer Motion/ease tokens.

## Ownership and limits

- The pending send intent is the preview producer. No persisted history, transport payload or protected media contains preview bytes or URLs.
- At most eight previews, three MiB each and twelve MiB combined. Eviction revokes URLs and publishes a bounded presentation change. One expiry owner reclaims previews after thirty seconds; canonical image load releases sooner. Empty cache has no timer. Lock, startup/runtime replacement and current-owner stop clear synchronously.
- Existing clientId survives canonical acceptance. Component reads check the current owner predicate; receiving history never substitutes installed pack art for received bytes.
- No added native reads, polling or fabricated transfer progress. Unknown progress stays indeterminate. Existing 100ms measured progress, 180ms content opacity and 80ms reduced-motion opacity are retained; no idle/hidden decorative loop.

# labali-git-auto-commit-rewrite

## NEVER

- **Never fabricate diff content** or invent changes not present in `git diff` output — a fabricated commit message is worse than no message; it destroys trust in git history.
- **Never amend a previous commit** — always create a new commit. Amending rewrites history and can silently overwrite commits that others (or hooks) have already acted on.
- **Never use `--no-verify`** to bypass pre-commit hooks — the hooks are the project's safety net; bypassing them defeats their purpose and masks real issues.
- **Never write a body that only lists filenames** — `- update core.ts` tells nothing; name the intent behind the change, not the file that changed.

## Commit Type Selection

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New capability or behavior visible to users/agents |
| `fix` | Corrects wrong behavior (not just wrong output) |
| `docs` | Documentation, examples, references only — no behavior change |
| `chore` | Housekeeping: structure, config, scripts, CI — no behavior change |
| `refactor` | Code restructure with no behavior change |
| `improve` | Meaningful enhancement to existing behavior (not a new feature, not a bug fix) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Test additions or changes only |

**Scope selection:** use a scope when the change is confined to one clear subsystem — `fix(browser): ...`, `feat(skill): ...`. Omit scope for cross-cutting changes that span multiple subsystems.

**When types conflict:** if a commit spans both a behavior change and a structural change, use the behavior-change type (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) — structural changes are secondary to their purpose. If the two concerns are truly independent, split into two commits.

## Execution Contract

1. Inspect working tree changes (`git status --short`, `git diff --name-status`) before writing message.
2. Before writing the subject, determine: is this a behavior change (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) or a structural change (`docs`/`chore`/`refactor`)? This choice drives the type.
   Generate a commit message that is both clear and elegant:
   - Subject format: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` or `<type>: <subject>`
   - Subject is concise, action-oriented, and specific to the dominant change set.
   - Body contains 2-6 bullet points, each tied to real grouped changes from diff.
   - Avoid vague wording like only `update`/`align` when multiple meaningful changes exist.
   - **MANDATORY — load `examples/good.md` before writing the message** to calibrate quality. Load `examples/anti-pattern.md` if the draft message feels vague or generic.
3. Stage all changes with `git add -A`.
4. Commit once with the generated subject and body. The commit command MUST be prefixed with `LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1` so the repository's pre-commit hook recognizes it as skill-authorized:
   ```bash
   LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "..."
   ```
5. MUST run `<skill_base_dir>/scripts/clean_commit.sh` immediately after commit (non-optional).
   The skill base directory is provided in the `Base directory for this skill:` line at the top of the invocation header.
   `clean_commit.sh` may rewrite the subject — read the final hash and subject from its output, not from the original commit.

## Message Quality Rules

- Body bullets must reflect actual file-level intent, not generic placeholders.
- Prefer aggregate summaries when many files changed, then include concrete sub-actions in body.

## Failure Handling

- If repository is not a Git repo, fail fast with explicit message.
- If there are no changes to commit, return `No changes to commit.`.

**CHANGES NEEDED.** Three important findings. No critical issues.

- **Pending videos show conflicting statuses.** An outgoing `.mp4` enters the inline player before it has a file ID. The parent displays “Preparing” while the player displays “Waiting for file.” The video placeholder should honor the parent’s transfer status. [MessageBubble.tsx](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/reception-source-pr-20261117/frontend/src/features/chat/MessageBubble.tsx:184>) · [MediaPreview.tsx](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/reception-source-pr-20261117/frontend/src/features/chat/MediaPreview.tsx:625>)
- **Failed outgoing photos can appear to be waiting for receipt.** When a native-path photo fails before admission, it has no local preview or file ID. The image stage shows a receiving status, and the footer suppresses the failure text because metadata is pending. The row should show the send failure and Retry. [MediaPreview.tsx](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/reception-source-pr-20261117/frontend/src/features/chat/MediaPreview.tsx:609>) · [MessageBubble.tsx](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/reception-source-pr-20261117/frontend/src/features/chat/MessageBubble.tsx:934>)
- **The staged photo path bypasses the static image pixel ceiling.** A 6000 × 4000 PNG can fit below 3 MiB while exceeding the documented 16,777,216-pixel limit. The new path assigns the original Blob URL to an image before checking its dimensions. Admission should use verified dimensions and show the preparing stage for oversized or unverified images. # Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

Guide completion of development work by presenting clear options and handling chosen workflow.

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## The Process

### Step 1: Verify Tests

**Before presenting options, verify tests pass:**

```bash
# Run project's test suite
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:**
```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]

Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass.
```

Stop. Don't proceed to Step 2.

**If tests pass:** Continue to Step 2.

### Step 2: Determine Base Branch

```bash
# Try common base branches
git merge-base HEAD main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD master 2>/dev/null
```

Or ask: "This branch split from main - is that correct?"

### Step 3: Present Options

Present exactly these 4 options:

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
4. Discard this work

Which option?
```

**Don't add explanation** - keep options concise.

### Step 4: Execute Choice

#### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Switch to base branch
git checkout <base-branch>

# Pull latest
git pull

# Merge feature branch
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>

# If tests pass
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
# Push branch
git push -u origin <feature-branch>

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<2-3 bullets of what changed>

## Test Plan
- [ ] <verification steps>
EOF
)"
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

**Don't cleanup worktree.**

#### Option 4: Discard

**Confirm first:**
```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for exact confirmation.

If confirmed:
```bash
git checkout <base-branch>
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

### Step 5: Cleanup Worktree

**For Options 1, 2, 4:**

Check if in worktree:
```bash
git worktree list | grep $(git branch --show-current)
```

If yes:
```bash
git worktree remove <worktree-path>
```

**For Option 3:** Keep worktree.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | ✓ | - | - | ✓ |
| 2. Create PR | - | ✓ | ✓ | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | ✓ | - |
| 4. Discard | - | - | - | ✓ (force) |

## Common Mistakes

**Skipping test verification**
- **Problem:** Merge broken code, create failing PR
- **Fix:** Always verify tests before offering options

**Open-ended questions**
- **Problem:** "What should I do next?" → ambiguous
- **Fix:** Present exactly 4 structured options

**Automatic worktree cleanup**
- **Problem:** Remove worktree when might need it (Option 2, 3)
- **Fix:** Only cleanup for Options 1 and 4

**No confirmation for discard**
- **Problem:** Accidentally delete work
- **Fix:** Require typed "discard" confirmation

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Proceed with failing tests
- Merge without verifying tests on result
- Delete work without confirmation
- Force-push without explicit request

**Always:**
- Verify tests before offering options
- Present exactly 4 options
- Get typed confirmation for Option 4
- Clean up worktree for Options 1 & 4 only

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **subagent-driven-development** (Step 7) - After all tasks complete
- **executing-plans** (Step 5) - After all batches complete

**Pairs with:**
- **using-git-worktrees** - Cleans up worktree created by that skill

item.aggregated_output:
Another known network device, including an infrastructure device when the role
permits it. A peer is not necessarily a person or a channel member.
_Avoid_: user, contact, member as interchangeable names.

**Contact**:
An account represented in local conversation/contact state. Contact visibility
is separate from discovery, delivery permission and channel membership.
_Avoid_: online peer, accepted member.

**Desktop session**:
One authenticated local user's login lifetime. A subsequent login starts a new
lifetime even when it belongs to the same local user.
_Avoid_: transport session, ratchet session, account lifetime.

**Participant runtime**:
The active network-participation lifetime of an initialized node. It is distinct
from persistent device identity and the host's login lifetime.
_Avoid_: device, desktop session.

An authorization for a local client to perform specified integration operations
for permitted destinations within its validity period.
_Avoid_: channel membership, device certificate, session token.

## Conversations and history

**Personal conversation removal**:
An account-private decision to remove a chat, optionally erasing its history on
certified linked devices. Durable deletion floors prevent stale private replay;
each device confirms its own cleanup separately. It is distinct from leaving or
dissolving a group, recalling a message and blocking a contact.
_Avoid_: global deletion, completed cleanup based only on a committed group Leave.
See [removal semantics](docs/network-design-reference.md#personal-conversation-removal).

**Conversation**:
A direct or channel conversation whose authorized content can be retained and
synchronized. A UI conversation selection is a view of that conversation.
_Avoid_: transport connection, multicast group.

**Direct message (DM)**:

**CHANGES NEEDED.** Three important findings remain in the reviewed candidate.

- **A contact with retained legacy chat history can expire.** The eligibility query checks the account-pair conversation ID. A verified device can have readable messages under a separate device-pair ID, as an existing search test demonstrates. The expiry check needs to include that evidence, including when the device is offline. [Eligibility query](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/empty-contact-expiry-20261118/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/queries.rs:23>) · [Existing fixture](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/empty-contact-expiry-20261118/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/search_tests.rs:705>)
- **A clock rollback can restore an expired contact.** Once an account disappears, a subsequent refresh with the clock just before its deadline makes it visible again. Persisting the first completed expiry would keep it hidden across clock corrections and restarts until chat history appears. [Expiry decision](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/empty-contact-expiry-20261118/src-tauri/src/contact_policy/expiry.rs:118>)
- **Repeated messages from an undiscovered device can trigger a full contact read per event.** The coordinator coalesces overlapping reads. Events spaced just beyond each read still trigger repeated native roster and identity queries. The existing two-second throttle covers peer discovery only. [Message invalidation](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/empty-contact-expiry-20261118/frontend/src/store/chat.ts:1810>) · [Unknown sender path](</Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/empty-contact-expiry-20261118/frontend/src/store/chat.ts:2498>)

I independently ran 13 focused frontend deadline, arrival, and stale-read tests. All passed. No critical findings.

Payload:
Read-only findings:

- `direct_held=true` means the exact destination device durably retains the encrypted event. It does not prove plaintext acceptance or a receipt.
- `relay_held=true` means an office retains the recipient-specific opaque wrapper. It does not establish recipient delivery.
- Only a validated recipient receipt, durably saved and applied through `mark_delivered_for`, clears Awaiting. Binding includes exact account, device and original event ID.

A concrete candidate deserves a focused regression: ordinary DM history reconciliation can block receipt retrieval. `transfer_delivery_destination` requires the full history round before Have; receipt-control sync follows only when that succeeds. Independent reconciliation also performs messages before receipts within one deadline, and requires verified-peer eligibility. Test an inbound-only recipient that genuinely received the original while subsequent DM-history work stalls, but receipt-control serving remains healthy.

Other unresolved candidates: exhausted shared TCP capacity, an unreachable route despite account-level Online status, an obsolete immutable recipient-device target, or receipt generation/application failing its durability or identity checks. The current logs cannot identify which message/device an attempt concerns.

Capacity is bounded at eight shared connections, seven outbound, two speculative historical dials, with two-second admission waits. Zero available permits proves pressure, not a leak or deadlock.

Useful existing selectors, not executed:

- `automatic_send_collects_receipt_when_recipient_can_only_serve_inbound_connections`
- `actual_durable_receive_sends_control_receipt_without_chat_callback`
- `receiver_write_failure_keeps_plaintext_intent_until_restart_and_no_early_receipt`
- `automatic_receipt_roundtrip_with_both_original_peers_stopped_in_turn`
- `historical_route_probes_leave_capacity_for_healthy_foreground_sync`
- `reachable_route_is_not_blocked_by_stalled_former_lan_handshake`

The three inspected production files match installed main376. No source changes, restricted-store reads, sends or builds performed.

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.
